data.name: Faq.Title
data.value: Answers for traders using COT and currency strength in real workflows

data.name: Faq.Description
data.value: These quick answers explain how TerminalPrime's forex tools fit into analysis, planning, and execution without turning the dashboard into noise.

data.name: Faq.Left1.Question
data.value: What is the COT report and why does it matter for forex traders?

data.name: Faq.Left1.Answer
data.value: The Commitment of Traders report shows how major futures participants are positioned. Traders often use it to understand longer-term sentiment, crowding, and possible reversals in currency markets.

data.name: Faq.Left2.Question
data.value: How often is the COT data updated?

data.name: Faq.Left2.Answer
data.value: COT data is published weekly, so it works best as a higher-timeframe context tool rather than a tick-by-tick signal feed.

data.name: Faq.Left3.Question
data.value: How should I combine COT with currency strength?

data.name: Faq.Left3.Answer
data.value: Use COT to understand broader positioning and use currency strength to confirm shorter-term leadership, weakness, and momentum changes.

data.name: Faq.Left4.Question
data.value: Which markets are covered in the COT section?

data.name: Faq.Left4.Answer
data.value: The dashboard groups available instruments by market so you can move quickly through major futures contracts and the report model you want to review.

data.name: Faq.Left5.Question
data.value: Is this useful for swing traders as well as day traders?

data.name: Faq.Left5.Answer
data.value: Yes. Swing traders can use COT for directional context, while day traders can use currency strength and broker checks to refine execution timing.

data.name: Faq.Right1.Answer
data.value: Yes. The dashboards are designed to make positioning and strength data easier to read, while the supporting content explains how the tools fit into a real workflow.

data.name: Faq.Right2.Question
data.value: Does currency strength update more often than COT?

data.name: Faq.Right2.Answer
data.value: Yes. Currency strength is designed for more frequent monitoring, while COT provides the slower, structural context behind the move.

data.name: Faq.Right3.Question
data.value: Do broker reviews matter for analysis?

data.name: Faq.Right3.Answer
data.value: They matter for execution. Even the best market read can suffer if spreads, slippage, or platform stability are poor during active sessions.

data.name: Faq.Right4.Answer
data.value: No. TerminalPrime is a research and analytics workspace. You should still apply your own risk management and decision process before trading.

data.name: Faq.Right5.Question
data.value: Can I use these tools as part of a weekly prep routine?

data.name: Faq.Right5.Answer
data.value: That is one of the best ways to use them. Review the broader positioning first, scan strength changes next, then build your levels and watchlist for the week.
